chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who leads a group in prayer, and another group joins his prayer after he has completed one rak'ah or more than that. When he finishes his prayer and gives the salam, is it permissible for him, while he is the Imam, to rise from his place before those who joined finish their prayer? He said, 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is to be understood as indicating concession (rukhsah), but the preferable course, which we have previously mentioned, is that he should wait until those behind him complete what they missed. To clarify this further, here is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: Can an Imam leave the prayer before latecomers finish joining him?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of an Imam departing before latecomers complete their *rak'ahs*, while Shaykh al-Tusi notes that the preferred etiquette (*afdhal*) is to wait for them to finish. This ruling highlights the balance between legal validity and communal harmony in congregational prayer, a key theme in Shia fiqh regarding the rights of the *muqtadi* (congregant).
